children: Indonesia's consumer inflation picked up in August as food prices rose.

The headline consumer-price index rose 3.19% from a year earlier, accelerating from July's 2.88% increase, driven by higher prices in the food, beverage and cigarette category, as well as increased personal-care and transport costs, the statistics agency said Tuesday. Core inflation was 2.92%, compared with 2.76% in July.
Inflation should remain within Bank Indonesia's 1.5%-3.5% target range, reflecting contained underlying price pressures, ANZ economist Dhiraj Nim said in a recent note.
A modest rise in August inflation is unlikely to materially alter BI's policy stance, with the central bank expected to prioritize rupiah stability amid external uncertainty, Nim said.
Still, risks remain from higher global energy prices and weather-related supply disruptions.
The Asean+3 Macroeconomic Research Office expects Indonesia's inflation to average 3.4% in 2026, within the central bank's target range.

Subsidized energy prices should cushion the impact of higher global oil prices, though inflation could come under pressure from rising energy costs, an El Niño-related hit to commodity production and the lagged effects of rupiah weakness, AMRO said in a recent note.
Under a more adverse scenario, inflation could temporarily exceed the target range, it added.
